note: The uSWID header length is read from attacker-controlled input and becomes part of later size calculations.
The payload length is also taken from the parsed header and drives how many bytes are exposed to later parsing.
The implementation records the total size without validating that hdrsz and payloadsz are consistent with the actual buffer bounds, allowing later reads to trust an oversized payload region.

code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
note: The parser reads payloadsz bytes starting at offset + hdrsz, so an inflated payloadsz can carry attacker-controlled length into the payload buffer.

code: fw2 = fu_bytes_new_offset(payload, offset_tmp, payloadsz - offset_tmp, error);
note: The remaining-length calculation is used to create a subview for coSWID parsing; when the payload bookkeeping is wrong, this can expose an out-of-bounds read in the downstream parser path.
